dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Cardinals Drop to 3-8 After Week 11 Defeat in Kansas City
dailyTopNewsBrief.summary: Arizona fell to 3-8 following a 34-7 road loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, highlighting ongoing operational struggles across all phases. Head coach Mike LaFleur's squad ranks 31st in points allowed per game (29.4) with an NFL-worst -132 point differential.
bullets: Quarterback Josh Johnson completed a 2-yard touchdown pass to receiver Simi Fehoko for Arizona's lone score in a 34-7 defeat to Kansas City, as detailed by [azcardinals.com Official](https://www.azcardinals.com/news/as-josh-johnson-takes-turn-in-quarterback-shuffle-cardinals-fall-to-chiefs).

Rookie defensive lineman Walter Nolen III registered a 7-yard sack on Patrick Mahomes, while tight end Trey McBride hurdled a defender for extra yards, per film highlights from [azcardinals.com Video](https://www.azcardinals.com/video/highlight-walter-nolen-iii-takes-down-patrick-mahomes-for-sack) and [azcardinals.com Video](https://www.azcardinals.com/video/highlight-trey-mcbride-hurdles-defender-for-extra-yardage).

Rookie quarterback Carson Beck remained ruled out due to a back injury, leaving Arizona's signal-caller rotation thin behind Johnson heading into Week 12, according to [azcardinals.com Official](https://www.azcardinals.com/news/the-future-of-carson-beck-s-back-and-chiefs-aftermath-cardinals).

Sitting at 3-8 with a 0.3% playoff probability under defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, the Cardinals prepare for a Week 12 matchup against the 3-5-1 Washington Commanders, who hold key statistical advantages in turnover margin (+7 vs -1) and rushing defense (103.8 vs 129.9 yards allowed), noted by [ESPN NFL Nation](https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401873067).
